# LiFePO4 vs NMC Power Stations

**For almost everyone, LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice.** NMC only makes sense if light weight matters most and you'll rarely use the unit.

## The key differences

| | LiFePO4 (LFP) | NMC |
|---|---|---|
| **Rated cycle life (power stations)** | Usually 3,000–6,000 | Usually 500–1,000 |
| **Weight** | Heavier at the cell level | About 10–16% more Wh per lb in finished stations |
| **Safety if a cell fails** | Much milder (cooler, slower, often no flames) | Hotter, and can ignite |
| **Price** | Now the cheaper mainstream option | Mostly older or compact models |
| **Cold-weather charging** | Most won't charge below 32°F | Same |

## What actually matters

**1. Cycle life is the big one.** Used daily (van, off-grid, solar), a 500-cycle NMC unit reaches 80% capacity in about 1.4 years. A 3,000-cycle LFP unit takes about 8 years. If you only use it for a few outages a year, either chemistry will likely age out from time before it runs out of cycles. ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/), [powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc))
- Read the fine print: "4,000 cycles to 70%" promises less than "4,000 to 80%." ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/))

**2. The weight gap is smaller than you'd think.** NMC cells are much denser, but the case, inverter and fans weigh the same either way. In same-maker pairs, such as Jackery's Explorer 1000 vs 1000 v2, the LFP version is only slightly heavier per kWh. Some LFP models are even lighter per Wh than older NMC ones. ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/), [UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/))

**3. Safety.** In lab tests, LFP cells in thermal runaway peaked far cooler than NMC cells (about 259°C vs 731°C in one study) and released much less gas. ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)) That's a real plus for a unit kept indoors or in a vehicle. But LFP isn't "fireproof." In one overcharge study, LFP reached runaway *earlier* than NMC, though it failed less violently. ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)) Be skeptical of sites saying LFP "can withstand overcharging."

**4. Cost.** NMC no longer saves you money. One dataset shows a median of $0.55/Wh for LFP vs $0.95/Wh for NMC. ([powerstations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc))

**5. Cold weather is mostly a wash.** Some sites say LFP handles cold charging much better. In practice, most stations of either chemistry won't charge below 32°F, so check the manual for the model you're considering. ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/), [Enough Watts](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc))

## Quick decision guide
- **Daily or frequent use (van, RV, solar, off-grid):** LiFePO4.
- **Home backup kept indoors:** LiFePO4.
- **Light weekend use where weight matters:** either. Compare the actual weight and price of specific models.
- **Already own a working NMC unit:** keep using it.

## Example LFP pick
The **BLUETTI Elite 200 V2** is a 2,074 Wh LiFePO4 unit. It has a 2,600 W inverter, a 6,000-cycle rating to 80% and a 5-year warranty. It's listed at $899, or $854.05 with code **AFF5OFF**.
